deck_title: Lucas-Washburn sqrt(t) capillary porous wicking vs naive linear-time wetting front overshoot rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Richard Lucas (1918) & Edward Wight Washburn (1921) capillary porous wicking law (balancing Laplace capillary pressure 2*sigma*cos(theta)/r_p against Hagen-Poiseuille viscous drag 8*mu*L/r_p^2 so L * dL/dt = D_w / 2 and wetting front length scales as L_LW(t) = L_0 * sqrt(t/t_0) = L_0 * (1 + u), locking L_active / L_LW = 1.0000x across all 17 time stations u = sqrt(t/t_0) - 1 in [0.000, 1.000] / t/t_0 in [1.000, 4.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive constant-speed linear wicking (L_naive = L_0 * (t/t_0) = L_0 * (1 + u)^2, which overshoots wetting height by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Darcy-Poiseuille pore impedance quadrature.

not_for: Non-porous hydrophobic Teflon or polished metal surfaces where droplets bead without capillary penetration
